answers.evidence:
# Evidence
- Problem class: go-mcp-server-run-shutdown-wedge-jsonv2-decoder-newline-undrained
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-10-23T20:10:02.464Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description:
SYMPTOM: a JSON-RPC stdio MCP server test that asserts Run returns after stdin close wedges for exactly the test deadline (3.00s) under Go 1.27.3 while the same commit passes in 0.00s under Go 1.26.10. A board row attributed it to a goroutine parked on a concurrency semaphore send inside the per-request goroutine.

REFUTATION: the goroutine dump captured with runtime.Stack(all=true) at the deadline shows the Run goroutine in sync.WaitGroup.Wait at server.go:164 and the REQUEST goroutine parked in io.Pipe.write, reached from fmt.Fprintln in writeResponse at server.go:307 (via sendError -> handleRequest -> Run.func1). It was never on the semaphore send. Root cause: Run's post-EOF shutdown wait (s.wg.Wait) covered in-flight request goroutines that wrote responses INLINE to stdout, so the shutdown wait was hostage to the CLIENT consuming every response byte.

WHY ONLY ON THE NEWER TOOLCHAIN: go1.27.3 enables encoding/json v2 in the baseline, so json.Decoder issues a 64-byte first read (jsontext decode make([]byte,0,64)). The response value is 64 bytes plus a trailing newline; the decoder consumes exactly the value and never drains the newline, so the server's io.Pipe write of the newline never returns. go1.26.10's decoder uses minRead=512 and over-reads, hiding the wedge. So the defect is toolchain-sensitive (a NEWER toolchain exposing a latent coupling), not a toolchain-floor problem: bumping the floor does not fix it.

FIX: writeResponse marshals the response and queues the bytes on a bounded channel (cap = maxConcurrent) consumed by a dedicated responseWriter goroutine that owns every stdout write; serialization moves from a mutex-per-write to the single writer, preserving enqueue order. s.wg now covers handler completion only. A done channel (closed via sync.Once from Run's return or Shutdown) tells the writer to drain queued responses and exit. A blocked client write then parks the writer goroutine alone and can never hold Run or Shutdown open. No timeout was increased.

REGRESSION TEST: read exactly the response value bytes from the stdout pipe and never the trailing newline, then require Run to return within the wall-clock budget; proved RED (3.00s, with the dumped parked frame) against the pre-fix server and GREEN on both toolchains after the fix. The shared requireRunReturned helper now dumps all goroutine stacks at the deadline before failing, so the next occurrence is diagnosed by evidence rather than inference.

VERIFICATION: pre-fix base under GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3 FAIL 3.00s; post-fix PASS 0.00s and full package ok under both toolchains; repo short suite 51 packages ok, 0 FAIL; build/vet/gofmt clean; independent LLM judge re-ran the A/B, reproduced the red arm from the pre-fix source, and confirmed the 64-vs-512 decoder read in the toolchain sources.
signatures.environment: Linux amd64, Go 1.27.3 vs Go 1.26.10 (GOTOOLCHAIN switch), Go module github.com/<project>, package pkg/mcp
